newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's bourse pursues downward trend.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's bourse pursues downward trend.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange closed on Wednesday 0.72 percent lower with drops in most stocks except for largest-cap conglomerate ONA Group group, stockbrokers said.
The all-share index closed at 671.79 points from 676.66 points on the previous session.
"The market is slowing down but the drop is not significant, a broker at the Casablanca-based ABN-AMRO Finance said.
In the banking sector, Wafabank, fell 25 dirhams to 860 dirhams with 1,406 shares traded.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc fell eight dirhams to 870 dirhams with 1,740 shares traded.
Market blue-chip Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, lost 15 dirhams to 632 dirhams with 1,982 shares exchanged.
Cement firms Lafarge Ciments, Ciments de l'Oriental and Ciments du Maroc dropped respectively 88, 20 and 20 dirhams to 1,392, 677 and 670 dirhams.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, the second largest private conglomerate, remained at 765 dirhams with 4,716 shares changing hands.
ONA, which holds stakes in more than 80 firms, was up 24 dirhams to 829 dirhams with 2,087 shares traded.

Other gainers included Banque Marocaine du Commerce et de l'Industrie, up 12 dirhams to 487 dirhams, Credit firm Credor, 23 dirhams up to 818 dirhams, and Credit firm Maroc Leasing, which rose 12 dirhams to 432 dirhams.
Traded volume on the official market stood at 40 million dirhams divided into 33.6 million dirhams in share trading, 6.0 million in privatisation bonds and 327,000 dirhams in contracts.
On the over-the-counter market trade amounted to 3.5 million dirhams only, a broker said. -- Rabat newsroom +212-7 72 65 18
